summary: Tested invoicing + 13% HST end to end. Backend: new suite tests/test_invoices_hst.py passed 23/23 (run with -n 0). It covers the public rate card; one invoice per delivered stop, made from a real CSV import and today's route, with DL-xxxxxx numbers, correct lines/subtotal/HST/total and merchant/business snapshots; no duplicate on re-deliver or backend restart; no invoice for a failed stop; merchant listing, summary and filters, 403 for mer-2, 401 without login; billing address backfilled to existing invoices; PDF link and download (%PDF, text has DashLocal, invoice number, merchant, Subtotal, HST (13%, Ontario), total), 400 for a garbage token, 403 for another invoice's token; report-paid; admin list, confirm (keeps the shop's note), undo/not received, 400 for unpaid with no note, 403 for non-admin; business GET/PUT defaults and validation, with the snapshot changing on new invoices only; weekly email send-now (sent). Frontend (375x667): the landing Pricing card shows $8.00 / $1.25 per km after 5 km / +$6.00 and the note about CAD + 13% HST. In the merchant portal: invoices card, outstanding/paid totals, ALL/UNPAID/PAID filters, tap to expand lines/HST/total, DOWNLOAD PDF (real file DashLocal-DL-000006.pdf downloads), I PAID THIS -> note -> TELL DASHLOCAL I PAID (submit stays disabled until a note is typed) -> pill becomes PAYMENT REPORTED, billing address edit/save; old weekly bill card gone. Admin: INVOICES link -> /admin/invoices, TO CONFIRM · n, CONFIRM PAID, PAID tab with the shop's note, UNDO, NOT RECEIVED, UNPAID tab MARK PAID disabled until a note is typed, business form save plus error toasts for hst_pct 45 and an empty name. Regression: 2 legacy tests in test_store_rates_bills_paid.py now fail because they assert the old weekly-bill email shape; the tests are outdated, not the app (see action items). No deprecated Expo packages found.

minor.issue: Updates are not atomic: the loop updates invoices one by one and raises 400 when it reaches an invoice with no note, so earlier ids in the same request are already marked paid when the request returns 400. Validate all ids first, then update.
The invoice number is taken from the counter before insert. If a parallel call hits DuplicateKeyError, that number is used up and leaves a gap in the DL- sequence. Low risk.

invoice.date is the UTC date of delivered_at ([:10]), but report_window()/the weekly email use the SF TZ. An evening delivery is dated the next day and can count in the wrong week. The PDF also prints 'Delivered ... UTC', which is odd for an Ontario business.

ui_bugs.issue: The UNPAID filter shows only status=unpaid (2 rows), but the OUTSTANDING counter includes 'reported' invoices (3). Users may think an invoice disappeared. Consider an 'OUTSTANDING' filter, or include reported invoices under UNPAID.

The box shows whenever unpaid_count > 0, which includes reported invoices. If every outstanding invoice is already 'reported', SELECT ALL UNPAID selects nothing. The selected total is also computed only from the current filter's list, so it can show CA$0.00 after you switch filters while something is still selected.

action_items: Update outdated legacy tests in tests/test_store_rates_bills_paid.py: test_weekly_email_send_now expects bill_total > 0 from the old weekly bill (it is now the sum of this week's invoices, and the test's direct-DB 'pastdrop' has no invoice), and test_email_html_has_statement calls weekly_email_html with the old bill dict (KeyError 'count'). Rewrite them for the invoice-based weekly email.
Make /admin/invoices/mark-paid validate notes for all ids before writing anything, so a 400 never leaves invoices half updated.
Optional: date invoices in local time (America/Toronto or the app TZ) instead of UTC so they match the weekly report window.
Optional UX: let the UNPAID filter include 'reported', or rename it; hide SELECT ALL UNPAID when there is nothing unpaid to select.
Update the stale 'weekly bill' copy on the landing page, merchant sign-in and admin home, and the hardcoded 13% in the admin invoices header.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 4218 lines; the invoice block (lines ~3630-3860) should be split into its own module.
There are two tax configs: pricing.tax_pct (old weekly bill) and business.hst_pct (invoices). The old one is now unused for billing and may confuse admins on /admin/pricing.
create_invoice falls back to compute_fee at delivery time if stop.fee is missing. That is fine, but the price is then the current rate, not the rate when the order was placed.
backfill_invoices runs at startup over every delivered merchant stop (to_list(5000)), so the first run after a big import could be slow. It is idempotent: restart verified, no duplicates.
Old weekly bill code (BillCard money helper, PaymentConfirmSheet, /admin/merchants/{id}/bills/*) is still present; check whether it is dead code.

success_rate.backend: 100% (23/23 new invoice tests); legacy regression 40/42 (2 outdated tests)
